theorem_title: Parity compatibility fixes the refined product modulo four
natural_language_statement:
For natural parameters $L,\varepsilon,z$, put $A=4z+2\varepsilon+1$, $P=2^LA-1$, and $Q=3\cdot2^{L-2}A-1$. When $L<2$, the exponent $L-2$ uses truncated natural subtraction.

Assume $\varepsilon\le1$ and $\varepsilon\equiv L\pmod2$. Then

$$
3^LA\equiv1\pmod4.
$$

This supplies the exact two-halving guard in the refined parent construction; no lower bound on L is required.
formal_statement:
theorem CollatzWork.compatibleProduct_mod_four
    (L epsilon z : Nat) (hepsilon : epsilon ≤ 1)
    (hparity : epsilon % 2 = L % 2) :
    (3 ^ L * refinedA epsilon z) % 4 = 1 := by sorry
